title: Tailwise Pharmacy Dispensing Standard: Conditions on Every Fill
content:
*Pharmacist-in-charge practice standard.*

This standard governs when a fill of a Tailwise Pharmacy prescription may be dispensed and what each fill does to the prescription.

## 1. Conditions on the prescription

1.1 The prescription status is active when the fill is dispensed.

1.2 A fill also needs at least 1 fill remaining on the prescription.

1.3 A fill is dispensed only if its date is before the prescription's expiry date. Expiry is compared as calendar dates: a fill dated on the expiry date or later is refused. There is no grace period; the offset applied to the expiry date is 0 days.

## 2. Refill-too-soon date

2.1 A refill is dispensed no earlier than the class's refill-too-soon share of the previous fill's days' supply after the previous fill's dispense date, unless an early-refill override applies.

2.2 The earliest refill date is the previous fill's dispense date plus the previous fill's days' supply multiplied by the refill-too-soon share (as a percentage) and rounded up to a whole calendar day; a refill on that date is in time.

The dates and days' supply compared are those of the previous dispensed fill on the prescription's pharmacy ledger.

## 3. Size of a fill

3.1 The days' supply of one fill may not exceed the class's maximum days' supply per fill nor, for compounded preparations, the beyond-use days.

3.2 For controlled substances, the total days' supply dispensed on the prescription after the fill — the days' supply of its dispensed fills less that of fills credited back — may not exceed the class's lifetime days' supply limit.

3.3 A partial fill is allowed only where the class allows partial fills and, where the class counts a partial fill as a whole fill, it uses a whole fill.

3.4 The first compounded fill ships no earlier than the class's compounding lead time in business days after authorization.

## 4. Effect of a fill

4.1 Each dispensed fill lowers the fills remaining by one.

4.2 The fill that brings the fills remaining to 0 moves the prescription to refills exhausted.

4.3 Reaching the expiry date moves an active or refills-exhausted prescription to expired.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

**Refill-too-soon date.** Previous fill dispensed 2026-05-01 with 30 days' supply, class share 85 percent: 30 multiplied by 85 percent is 25.5, rounded up to 26 days. Earliest refill date 2026-05-27. A refill on 2026-05-27 is in time; a refill on 2026-05-26 is too soon unless an early-refill override applies.

**Same fill, share 75 percent.** 30 multiplied by 75 percent is 22.5, rounded up to 23 days; earliest refill date 2026-05-24.

**Expiry.** Expiry date 2026-09-10. A fill dated 2026-09-09 meets the expiry condition; a fill dated 2026-09-10 is refused.

**Lifetime limit (controlled substance, limit 180 days).** Fills of 30 days already dispensed total 150 days with none credited back. A further 30-day fill brings the total to 180 days and is within the limit; a fill bringing the total past 180 days is not.

| Status active | Fills remaining at least 1 | Fill date before expiry | Not too soon, or override applies | Result on these conditions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | all four met |
| No | any | any | any | refused |
| any | No | any | any | refused |
| any | any | No | any | refused |
| any | any | any | No | refused |
